metaDescription: Six EGO 56V cordless snow blowers compared, from a 12-inch shovel to a 28-inch two-stage, with battery, throw and driveway-size guidance.
expertTake: The 28-inch two-stage kit is the most capable battery machine in the EGO range, and the 24-inch XP is the sweet spot for most long driveways. The single-stage 21-inch models are the value pick for paved drives under about 60 feet. Skip the whole battery category if your snow is routinely wet, knee deep and arrives with a plow-berm at the end of the drive.
introParagraphs: A single battery platform is the main reason people shop one brand for snow removal. Packs charged for the mower in July can power the blower in January, and the charger, the cold-weather habits and the warranty paperwork are already familiar.

The catch is that battery snow blowers come in very different mechanical designs under one badge. Some scrape the pavement with a rubber auger and throw snow in one step, others use a two-stage auger and impeller. Knowing which design suits your drive matters more than any single spec.

products.name: EGO Power+ SNT2800 28-inch two-stage kit, 2 x 12Ah
products.description:
This is the widest machine EGO makes, a 28-inch two-stage with a 21-inch intake. A separate auger breaks the snow and an impeller flings it, which is why the listing claims up to 60 feet of throw. Peak Power mode combines both packs into one boosted output, so it is the closest a battery machine comes to the gas units it competes with.

The tradeoff is mass and the battery bill. Two 12Ah packs are the kit's real value and also its weight, and a 28-inch path is overkill for a two-car drive where the 24-inch XP does the same work with less machine to store. The listing quotes a 32-car driveway with 8 inches of snow on one charge, but that is a light dry-snow figure; wet snow will cut it hard. It is the pick for long drives, corner lots and anyone who wants fewer passes.

Ownership is simple: no fuel, no carburetor, no pull cord. Keep the packs indoors until you need them, because lithium output sags in deep cold, and clear the chute with the packs removed. The same ARC packs fit EGO mowers and trimmers, which is how a big kit like this pays back over several seasons.
products.bestFor: Long or wide driveways where cutting the number of passes matters most.
pros: Widest path in the EGO line at 28 inches
Throws up to 60 feet from a two-stage system
Big 12Ah packs cover long drives per charge
No fuel, oil or carburetor to maintain
cons: Heavy and bulky for short drives and tight garages
Highest cost of entry because of the large packs

products.name: EGO Power+ 24-inch two-stage XP kit, 2 x 10Ah
products.description:
The XP kit puts the 24-inch two-stage chassis together with two 10Ah packs, which the listing rates for a 24-car driveway with 8 inches of snow. The chassis matches the 7.5Ah kit below, so what you are paying for is runtime rather than a different machine. Variable-speed self-propel and a 20-inch intake handle deep snow without the operator pushing.

Against the 28-inch model it gives up 4 inches of width and 10 feet of throw, but it is lighter to move around the garage and needs the same packs only in smaller capacity. Against the 7.5Ah kit it simply carries about a third more watt-hours, which is the right trade if your drive is long or you clear for neighbours.

Expect the usual battery habits: charge the packs indoors, let a cold pack warm to room temperature before the first pass, and slide the second pack in only when the first is spent. Shear-pin style jams are rare, but if the auger stalls on a frozen berm, pull the packs before clearing it.
products.bestFor: Two-stage performance with extra runtime for drives that run long.
pros: Two 10Ah packs cover long drives per charge
Two-stage auger and impeller clears deep snow
Self-propelled drive saves the operator effort
Same chassis as cheaper 24-inch kit, upgraded runtime
cons: Costs more than the 7.5Ah kit for the same machine
Still less capacity than the 28-inch on very large lots

products.name: EGO SNT2405 24-inch two-stage kit, 2 x 7.5Ah
products.description:
The SNT2405 is the baseline 24-inch two-stage, and for most homeowners it is the sensible entry to the EGO range. It shares its 20-inch intake and 50-foot throw with the XP kit, and the listing rates it for an 18-car driveway with 8 inches of snow on two packs.

Compared with the 10Ah XP kit it has about 25 percent less stored energy, so it suits a typical two to four car drive rather than a long lane. It is also one of the older designs in the lineup, which means fewer surprises in owner reports and easy availability of replacement parts and packs.

A two-stage machine of this size is easier to push through a berm than a single-stage because the impeller does the throwing while the wheels do the pulling. Store it with the packs removed, wipe the chute down after wet snow and keep the auger housing free of ice slush so the auger does not freeze to the housing overnight.
products.bestFor: Families with a typical suburban drive wanting two-stage capability without the biggest kit.
pros: Two-stage power at a lower entry point than the XP
Throws up to 50 feet from the chute
Self-propelled drive reduces fatigue
Packs interchange with other EGO outdoor tools
cons: Runtime tops out sooner than the 10Ah and 12Ah kits
Not as light as a single-stage for short paved drives

products.name: EGO Power+ SNT2122 21-inch single-stage, 2 x 4Ah
products.description:
A single-stage machine uses one rubber-edged auger that contacts the pavement, pulls the machine forward and throws the snow in a single motion. The SNT2122 adds variable auger speed and a 180-degree chute, and the listing rates two 4Ah packs for a 10-car driveway with 8 inches of snow.

That design is lighter and cheaper than a two-stage and clears paved drives right down to the surface, but it will not climb a plow berm or chew through heavy crust. It also grabs gravel, so keep it off stone drives. Against the 6Ah 21-inch model below it simply has smaller packs and a shorter 42-foot throw.

There is no wheel drive, which means the machine moves itself forward only by the auger biting in. On slippery packed surfaces it can walk sideways, so go slowly. Wipe the scraper bar and check the rubber paddles for wear before each season; they are the main consumable.
products.bestFor: Paved drives and walks up to a few car lengths with light to moderate snow.
pros: Lighter and easier to store than a two-stage
Variable auger speed matches snow depth
Peak Power boosts output when both packs run
180-degree chute with up to 42 feet of throw
cons: Struggles with heavy crust and plow berms
Auger paddles wear and will throw gravel

products.name: EGO Power+ 21-inch single-stage, 2 x 6Ah
products.description:
This 21-inch model pairs a steel auger with two 6Ah packs and is rated by the maker for a 14-car driveway with 8 inches of snow. Throw is quoted at up to 45 feet, 3 feet more than the SNT2122, which is a modest gain from the larger packs.

The steel auger resists chipping better than a rubber-only design when it meets frozen slush or an ice ridge left by a plow. Even so it is a single-stage, so expect to take a second pass on heavy snow and keep your expectations realistic on anything deeper than about 8 inches.

It makes the most sense for owners with a drive of three to six cars who do not want the footprint of a two-stage. Pack storage matters here: keep both batteries indoors between storms so the first pass is not at winter-garage temperature.
products.bestFor: Owners wanting longer single-stage runtime without moving up to a two-stage.
pros: Steel auger tolerates frozen slush better than rubber
6Ah packs give meaningful runtime headroom
Up to 45 feet of throw
Brushless motor with no brushes to replace
cons: Single-stage will not climb heavy berms
Costs more than the 4Ah single-stage for a modest gain

products.name: EGO Power+ SNS1201 12-inch cordless snow shovel
products.description:
The SNS1201 is a lightweight powered shovel, not a snow blower in the usual sense. A narrow 12-inch auger path and a dial-adjusted 60-degree deflector let it clear steps, decks and short walks that a full machine cannot turn around on.

The included 2.5Ah pack is rated for roughly a 3-car driveway in 6 inches of snow, which tells you where its limit is. If you already own other EGO ARC packs, it is a cheap add-on and lets you use a bigger pack when you need more time.

Its value is in being the tool you grab for the porch, steps and patio, while a bigger EGO handles the drive. It will bog in heavy, wet snow, so clear in lighter passes and avoid forcing it into drifts.
products.bestFor: Steps, decks and small walkways where a full machine will not fit.
pros: Light enough to use one-handed on steps
Dial adjusts chute direction while you work
Uses the same EGO ARC packs as the big blowers
Throws up to 25 feet
cons: Only a 12-inch path, so driveways take a long time
Bogs down in deep or heavy wet snow

buyingCriteria.explanation: A single-stage uses a rubber-tipped auger that touches the ground and throws snow itself, which is why the SNT2122 is lighter but limited to about 8 inches. A two-stage like the 24-inch SNT2405 adds an impeller, a wheel drive and a 20-inch intake that handles deeper snow and plow berms. The common mistake is buying a single-stage for a long gravel or heavily plowed drive, then returning it after the first big storm. Match design to your deepest typical snowfall, not the average.

Volts do not set runtime; amp-hours do. The XP kit's two 10Ah packs carry roughly a third more energy than the SNT2405's two 7.5Ah, and the 28-inch kit's two 12Ah packs carry the most. Maker ratings assume light dry snow, so cut them by half or more for wet heavy snow. If you have a long drive, size packs up before you size the machine up.

Width sets how many passes you make; intake height sets how deep a single pass can go. The 28-inch kit moves 4 inches more per pass than the 24-inch XP and has a 21-inch intake against 20. Wider is heavier and harder to store, so a two-car drive rarely benefits from the 28.

The 28-inch kit claims up to 60 feet, the 24-inch two-stages up to 50 and the 21-inch single-stages 42 to 45. Longer throw means less re-clearing when wind blows snow back, but it only matters if the chute is easy to turn. The SNS1201's dial controls direction on a small tool, while the larger machines use a hand crank or lever.

Lithium cells deliver far less output near 0 F, and a cold-soaked pack will also charge slowly. Store the packs inside and insert them just before the first pass. This matters more for the 12Ah and 10Ah kits, which are expensive packs that you want to keep healthy for the next mower season.

EGO ARC packs are shared across the maker's mowers, trimmers and blowers, so an existing 5Ah or 7.5Ah pack can power a kit-less purchase like the SNT2420 or SNT2120 tool-only models. If you do not already own the platform, the bundled-kit models are the sensible choice because they include the chargers and packs needed to actually run the machine.

specDecoder.meaning: A boost mode where two packs combine into a single higher output. It is why the maker says these machines rival gas.
specDecoder.watchFor: It drains packs faster, so large kits like the 28-inch with 12Ah packs benefit most.

specDecoder.meaning: Battery capacity at a given voltage. Multiplying Ah by 56V gives a rough watt-hour figure for comparing packs.
specDecoder.watchFor: Compare the 4Ah SNT2122 kit against the 10Ah XP kit before assuming they run for the same time.

specDecoder.meaning: A maker figure assuming 8 inches of snow of a specific type. It is a rough ceiling, not a promise.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 28-inch kit's 32-car figure will shrink with wet snow or heavy berms.

specDecoder.meaning: How tall a snow bank the auger housing can take in one pass.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 28-inch has a 21-inch intake; the 24-inch units a 20-inch intake, so drifts deeper than that need two lifts.

specDecoder.meaning: Single-stage throws snow with the auger; two-stage separates breaking and throwing.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 21-inch models are single-stage and will not self-propel through a berm.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mechanical design
howWeEvaluated.description: We sorted the lineup into single-stage, two-stage and powered-shovel designs, since that decides what snow depth each can realistically handle. We then compared clearing width, intake height and drive type. We did not rate a machine against jobs its design cannot do.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery energy
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared pack amp-hours and kit configuration rather than voltage alone. The 7.5Ah, 10Ah and 12Ah kits are meaningfully different in stored energy even though the chassis is shared. We flagged which kits include chargers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Throw and clearing capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We used the maker's stated throw distances and cars-per-charge figures as relative comparisons, from 25 feet for the shovel to 60 feet for the 28-inch. We treated those as best-case figures for light dry snow.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership burden
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns, we weighed what each model asks of you: storing batteries indoors, replacing paddles on the single-stages, clearing jams safely. Battery machines remove fuel and carburetor work but add pack care.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit to household
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched each model to a driveway size and snow type, so the 12-inch shovel suits steps while the 28-inch suits long drives. This is an editorial assessment, not a measured score.

cards.label: Single-stage
cards.text: The SNT2122 and 6Ah 21-inch model use one auger that touches the pavement. They are lighter, simpler and clear paved surfaces down to the ground, but they walk sideways on ice and will not climb a berm.

cards.label: Two-stage
cards.text: The SNT2405, XP and SNT2800 separate the auger from the impeller and add wheel drive. They handle deep snow and plow berms but are heavier and need more garage space.

howToChoose.note: Pick single-stage for paved drives under about 60 feet; choose a two-stage once the drive is long, gravel or regularly buried.

rows: More energy for the same chassis

howToChoose.subheading: For Gravel and Heavy Plow Berms Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A two-stage with adjustable skid shoes and a high intake, so the auger housing sits above the stones. Single-stage augers throw gravel and are not suitable.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The EGO SNT2405 and XP kit are the two-stage options with a 20-inch intake. Raise the skid shoes on gravel and plan on a berm-breaking first pass.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a long drive, need to clear for neighbours or live where storms arrive back to back. The XP kit's 10Ah packs or the SNT2800's 12Ah packs reduce mid-job pauses to charge.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have a short paved drive. The SNT2122 or the SNS1201 shovel will do the work, and you can add packs later if your needs grow.

maintenance.why: Cold cuts lithium output and can slow charging. Store at partial charge in a dry place.
Single-stage paddles wear thinner with every pass. Replace them when the edge stops contacting the pavement.
Skid shoes set the auger height. Worn shoes let the housing hit the surface.
A stalled auger can restart without warning. Never use hands.
Slush freezes overnight and stiffens the chute. A quick wipe prevents the next start from jamming.

faq.a: A single-stage is lighter and clears pavement cleanly but cannot climb a berm. A two-stage handles deeper snow and wheel-driven travel. Choose by drive length and snow depth.

faq.q: How much does a 12Ah pack matter?
faq.a: It gives the most runtime, which is the real limit on long drives. A big pack also adds weight and cost, so it is worth it only when you actually need the extra minutes.

faq.q: Can I use my mower packs?
faq.a: Yes, EGO ARC packs are shared across the line. The tool-only SNT2120 and SNT2420 models assume you have two compatible packs, so check capacity before buying a tool-only unit.
It is a maker estimate for 8 inches of snow under ideal conditions. Wet heavy snow, berms and steep drives will shorten it, so treat it as a best case.

faq.q: Will it work in deep cold?
faq.a: Lithium cells lose output near 0 F. Keep packs indoors until use and let them settle to room temperature if they were cold-soaked.
No. The auger scrapes the surface and throws loose stones. Use a two-stage with raised skid shoes on gravel.
